start.content:
My name is Eleazar. I am a son of Aaron — not by birth, but by
contract. The Temple employs my family to manage its commercial
interests. What you call the "Triumphal Entry," I call an
unauthorized seizure of property. The colt was not lent. It was
taken. By force. Under cover of religious fervor.

choices.text: You filed a complaint with the authorities.
The owner says he gave it willingly.
You witnessed the Temple cleansing too.

complaint.content:
I witnessed the entire event from my villa's upper terrace. Two
rough-looking men approached the tethering post near the gate.
They drew blades — crude iron points — and hacked through the
rope. The owner protested. Violently. I have the guards'
testimony to corroborate my deposition.

choices.text: The rope fibers show no cuts.
You had a view but not the full picture.

willing_owner.content:
Tobias is a dreamer. He sees prophecies in every bird that flies
over his field and every breeze that stirs his curtains. When I
questioned him, he insisted the colt was "given freely" and that
the stranger's words — "The Lord needs it" — unlocked some ancient
recognition. I have studied the Torah for forty years, not folk tales.

choices.text: Tobias is not qualified to testify.

temple_cleansing.content:
Three days later, the same crowd that celebrated a stolen donkey
demanded that I explain why our Temple had become a marketplace.
I stood in the outer courts and watched a Galilean carpenter
destroy three centuries of established commerce with nothing
but a whip of rushes. He called it "cleansing." I call it
economic terrorism.

rope_evidence.content:
The rope fibers, examined under magnification, show fresh
separation at the cut points. Iron residue on the remaining
strands. The owner's claim that he "untied" the colt is
physically impossible. I am a man of evidence, not superstition.

choices.text: But you were in your villa.
You have not examined the scene.

owner_contradicts.content:
Yes. Tobias contradicts my deposition. He claims the colt was
"lent willingly." I have reviewed his testimony. He is either
lying or delusional. A man who believes Zechariah's prophecy
walks off the page cannot be trusted with legal testimony.

choices.text: Your income depends on Temple commerce.

partial_view.content:
I had a villa overview. Not the ground-level detail. But I
saw the approach, the confrontation, the removal of the
animal. The crowd's reaction. The owner's protest. From
two hundred cubits up, I had sufficient perspective to
file an accurate deposition.

discredit_owner.content:
Tobias tends barley fields outside the city walls. He is a
simple farmer. He deals in metaphors and folk wisdom. I
deal in contracts, in legal precedents, in the kind of
evidence that survives scrutiny in a Roman court of law.

choices.text: The simple can see what the wise miss.
Your education has not prepared you for this.

perjury.content:
Perjury? My deposition is sworn testimony. I stand by every
word. If the owner's memory fails him under pressure, that
does not invalidate my account. Two temple guards confirm
they heard the owner's protest. My word against his fantasy.

choices.text: Your guards are paid by you.

zealot_discredit.content:
Call it what you will — a dreamer, a zealot, a fool carrying
old scrolls and talking about kings and prophecies. The point
remains: property was removed without proper authorization.
The Sanhedrin has already taken my deposition seriously enough
to open an inquiry.

choices.text: The inquiry favors the donkey's owner.

temple_support.content:
I support the established order. The Temple is not merely
a religious institution — it is the economic engine of
Judea. Without its commercial operations, the priesthood
cannot function. Without the priesthood, the people lose
their connection to the covenant.

choices.text: Profit motives are incompatible with worship.

legal_licenses.content:
Every merchant in the Court of the Gentiles operates under
priestly license. Every transaction is registered. Every
animal is inspected. We maintain standards that a carpenter
from Nazareth cannot comprehend.

choices.text: The licenses are bought and sold.

fear_disruption.content:
I fear what the crowd will do if left to their own devices.
Today it is a whip and scattered coins. Tomorrow it could
be actual violence. The Romans do not distinguish between
religious enthusiasm and political rebellion. They respond
to both with legions.

choices.text: The Romans will be called in.
The real threat is the king.

investment_protection.content:
My family has invested three generations of wealth in
this Temple operation. My father, my grandfather, and
my son all draw income from the commercial activities.
A man who threatens that enterprise threatens not just
my livelihood but my family's security. I am protecting
what is mine by inheritance.

choices.text: What is the kingdom of God worth?
Your investment is in the wrong place.

income_dependence.content:
My income depends on the Temple's stability, just as
every Jerusalem merchant depends on its prosperity.
The Galilean's "cleansing" disrupted a system that
functioned for two thousand years. I was protecting
the livelihood of hundreds of families.

choices.text: The poor need access, not protection of profit.

dismissal_tactic.content:
I am not dismissing him as delusional. I am dismissing
his claims as unfounded. A man who says he is the
fulfillment of Zechariah's prophecy bears the burden
of proof. An unridden donkey does not make a king.
Peaceable entry does not establish divine authority.

choices.text: The proof is in the crowd's recognition.
Signs and wonders are not political evidence.

sanhedrin_divided.content:
The Sanhedrin is indeed divided. Caiaphas sees political
threat. The Pharisees see theological concern. Some
scribes see genuine prophecy. But the Sadducees — those
who control the Temple finances — see the greatest
threat to the established order. I am not alone.

choices.text: The Sadducees have the most to lose.

using_deposition.content:
They use my deposition because it is accurate. I am not
a religious extremist. I am not a zealot. I am a
businessman who witnessed unauthorized property seizure
and filed the appropriate report. If my testimony
threatens their position, that is their problem.

choices.text: You twist facts to fit conclusions.

inquiry_favors.content:
The inquiry is ongoing. The owner's testimony has
not yet been cross-examined under oath. When it is,
the inconsistencies will emerge. A man who claims
"the Lord needs it" speaks of divine mandate, not
property transfer.

choices.text: Your concern is legal, not spiritual.
The law and the gospel conflict.

alibi_issue.content:
I was in my villa. My servants confirm it. But the
deposit boxes at the Antonia fortress have guards on
rotation. Their testimony supports the timing of
the incident. I had adequate observation to file
a credible deposition.

owner_clear.content:
The owner's eyes were clear. Perhaps too clear.
Perhaps drugged. Perhaps delirious with religious
ecstasy. I have seen farmers who have worked too
long in the sun. Their perceptions grow...
unreliable.

choices.text: You seek to discredit all witnesses.

scene_unexamined.content:
I have not examined the scene personally. But I
employ investigators. The report from my agent
confirms the iron residue on the rope fibers.
The cut marks are visible under magnification.
I trust those who examine details.

bought_licenses.content:
The licenses are purchased through proper channels
and renewed annually. The fees support the priestly
families who maintain the Temple's sacred functions.
Without this revenue, the institution cannot operate.
Commerce and covenant are not opposites — they
are partners.

cursory_inspection.content:
The inspections are cursory. The priests are old.
The standards are... flexible. Animals that would
be rejected in any other market are accepted here
because the buyers are pilgrims who cannot afford
to be picky.

overcharging.content:
The poor bring what little they have. We provide
what they need. The prices reflect the reality
of Temple commerce — transportation, inspection,
maintenance, security. If they cannot afford
our prices, they can pray from outside the gates.

choices.text: You have turned worship into commerce.

roman_response.content:
The Romans will be called in when the crowds
become unruly. Today it is scattered coins.
Tomorrow — when the people realize their
leader has been taken — it could be stones.
Or worse. I prefer order to chaos.

misplaced_fear.content:
My fear is not misplaced. I have lived in
Jerusalem long enough to know how quickly
crowds turn from celebration to violence.
The same people who shouted "Hosanna"
can just as easily shout "Crucify." I prefer
to be on the side of order.

choices.text: History judges those who choose order over righteousness.

real_threat.content:
The real threat is not the donkey or the whip.
The real threat is the claim that this man
— this carpenter — is the king God promised.
If the people believe that, they will abandon
the Temple. They will abandon us. They will
abandon everything that makes this city great.

choices.text: They abandon idols for the living God.

kingdom_worth.content:
What is the kingdom of God worth? It is worth
the cost of following it. The question you should
ask is: what is the Temple worth? What is the
established order worth? What is the system that
has served Israel for centuries worth?

choices.text: The price is measured in souls.

wrong_investment.content:
My investment is in the stability of Jerusalem.
In the prosperity of my family. In the Temple's
enduring relevance. These are not wrong
investments. They are wise ones.

choices.text: Your family's prosperity comes at a cost.
Investment in stone cannot save souls.

money_serving.content:
I serve the system that has provided for my
family for generations. I serve the Temple
that has been the centre of Jewish worship
for centuries. I serve the order that
prevents chaos. If that makes me a
"money-serving" man, then all of Jerusalem
serves money.

corruption_point.content:
Corruption in commerce? Of course there is corruption.
But corruption in faith? That is a different question
entirely. The Galilean speaks of love and forgiveness,
but He does not provide the means by which the Temple
functions. Without our commerce, how do the poor
offer their sacrifices?

choices.text: The system serves a purpose, but it can be reformed.

system_endurance.content:
The system has endured because it works.
Two thousand years of continuous operation.
Through Babylonian captivity. Through
Maccabean revolt. Through Roman occupation.
The Temple endures because it adapts while
remaining faithful to its core function.

choices.text: Endurance is not proof of truth.

worship_profit.content:
Worship without institutional support becomes
chaos. Profit without worship becomes greed.
We maintain the balance. We provide the
means by which worship can function in a
complex society. Remove the profit, and
worship becomes impossible.

parasite_question.content:
Parasites? The merchants, the priests, the
scribes, the guards — we all serve the
same purpose. We maintain the system
that allows worship to happen. Without
us, the pilgrims would have no sacrifices.
No offerings. No access to God.

choices.text: You are part of the problem.

poor_better.content:
The poor deserve better than a king who
rides on a donkey. They deserve a system
that provides predictable, reliable access
to the divine. Religious enthusiasm disrupts
that reliability.

exploitation_suffering.content:
Exploitation? The prices are set by
the market. The poor pay what they
can. Those who cannot afford the
offerings pray from outside the gates.
This is not exploitation — it is
economic reality.

choices.text: Economic reality is not moral reality.

system_corrupt.content:
Every institution has corruption. But
the system as a whole is not corrupt.
It is the individuals within it who
sometimes fail. The system provides
structure, order, predictability.

choices.text: The system protects itself, not the people.

exploit_pilgrims.content:
The pilgrims know the prices. They
understand the costs. They come
prepared. Those who are unprepared
are turned away — but that is their
responsibility, not ours.

choices.text: You shift blame to the victims.

system_allows.content:
The system allows what the market allows.
If the prices are too high, the pilgrims
will not come. But they do come.
Because they have no alternative.
And we provide the alternative they
need.

flexibility_corruption.content:
Flexibility in standards. Flexibility
in interpretation. Flexibility in
enforcement. These are not corruption —
they are the practical realities of
maintaining order in a complex society.

prayer_free.content:
Prayer does not require payment.
But sacrifice does. And sacrifice
requires animals. And animals
require Temple commerce. We
are not selling prayer — we
are enabling sacrifice.

choices.text: The system confuses means and ends.

access_free.content:
Access should not require payment.
But the animals do. The
inspection does. The Temple
maintenance does. We charge
for the service, not the
spiritual encounter.

worship_commerce.content:
You have turned worship into
commerce. We have turned
commerce into worship.
Different perspectives.
Same reality.

order_oppression.content:
Order is not oppression.
Order is the framework
within which freedom can
flourish. Without order,
there is only chaos.
And chaos serves no one.

chaos_fear.content:
The chaos is my fear.
The fear of what happens
when crowds believe a
carpenter is a king.
When enthusiasm replaces
discipline. When emotion
replaces order. When
the system that has
served Israel for
centuries is
thrown into
disarray.

choices.text: The system deserves to be thrown.

real_peace.content:
The king offers peace
through submission to
authority. My peace
through preservation of
the Temple system.
The king on a donkey
brings chaos. The
priest with contracts
brings order.

city_greatness.content:
What makes the city great
is its Temple. Its system.
Its order. Its predictability.
Its ability to serve
thousands of pilgrims each
year without chaos. The
king on a donkey threatens
that greatness.

choices.text: Stability without justice is not greatness.

temple_questioned.content:
The Temple's authority
is questioned by a man
who has never studied
the Torah. Who has
never served in the
priesthood. Who has
never managed the
complex logistics of
sacred service.

living_god.content:
They abandon idols for
the living God? What
they abandon is the
system that has
connected them to
the living God for
two thousand years.
A king on a donkey
cannot replace a
Temple.

choices.text: The Temple is replaced by the body.
Direct access through the living God.
A donkey is not an idol.

more_than_comfort.content:
More than comfort.
More than security.
More than tradition.
The cost is
everything. And
the reward is
eternity. What
is your
investment
worth?

more_than_tradition.content:
More than tradition.
More than ritual.
More than the
forms of worship
that have
preserved us
for centuries.
The king
demands
everything.
The Temple
demands
payment.
Choose.

choices.text: The king offers grace over payment.

souls_measured.content:
The price is measured
in souls. The system's
price. The king's
price. The Temple's
price. Which
price
will
you
pay?

choices.text: Grace is the only payment possible.

all_serve.content:
All of Jerusalem
serves the system.
All of Jerusalem
benefits from
the order.
All of Jerusalem
depends on
the Temple's
commercial
operations.
We are
partners
in
survival.

system_problem.content:
The system is the
problem? Or are
the people
within it?
A system is
a framework.
People are
the actors.
We act within
the constraints
we choose.

defend_corruption.content:
You say I
defend
corruption.
I say I
maintain
order.
You see
oppression.
I see
stability.
You see
greed.
I see
necessary
function.
We see
different
things
because
we
value
different
outcomes.

choices.text: Stability without righteousness is not stability.
You cannot defend what is indefensible.

direct_access.content:
Direct access
to God?
Through
what?
Through
faith?
Through
grace?
Through
a man
on a
donkey?
The
Temple
provides
the
means.
The
system
provides
the
structure.
The priest
provides
the
sacrament.

closing_eleazar.content:
I am Eleazar ben Simon.
I have filed my deposition.
I have stated my concerns.
I have defended the system
that has served Israel for
two thousand years. You
can believe me or not.
But you cannot deny
that I witnessed what
I witnessed. And I
will testify to it.
Whatever the cost.
